title.ko: 유머와 풍자: dry wit · pun · tongue-in-cheek · with a straight face
title.en: humour and sarcasm: dry wit, pun, tongue-in-cheek, with a straight face

explain.ko: 유머는 말장난(pun), 반어(irony), 풍자(satire), 과장, 절제 등으로 만들어집니다. 영국식 건조한 유머(dry humour)는 무표정(with a straight face)으로 말하는 것이 특징이고, tongue-in-cheek은 농담조의 말을 뜻합니다. 같은 농담도 문화와 관계에 따라 불쾌감을 줄 수 있으므로 눈치(tact)가 필요합니다. 풍자는 권력이나 사회를 비판하는 방식으로 쓰입니다.
explain.en: Humour is made through puns, irony, satire, exaggeration and understatement. British dry humour is typically delivered with a straight face, and tongue-in-cheek describes a joking, not-serious remark. The same joke can offend depending on culture and relationship, so tact is needed. Satire criticises power or society.

notes.ko: 농담이 오해를 부를 수 있으니 상황을 먼저 살피세요.
notes.en: Check the situation first; jokes can be misunderstood.
Sarcasm is hard to convey in writing.
Humour varies by culture; use it respectfully.

lines.t: British humour is often dry and ironic. Because it is delivered with a straight face, it is hard at first to tell serious from joking. Satire and self-deprecation are also key elements. You need to understand the culture to get it.

items.passage: British comedy often uses irony and (1). Actors deliver lines with a (2) face and the audience laughs as they catch the implication. Such humour can be hard for (3) to follow.

trans.ko: 영국의 코미디는 반어와 절제된 표현을 자주 사용합니다. 배우들은 무표정하게 대사를 말하고 관객은 그 속뜻을 알아채며 웃습니다. 이런 유머는 처음 접하는 사람에게는 이해하기 어려울 수 있습니다.

items.passage:
COLUMN
The art of laughter
A joke is received very differently depending on the person and situation. The same joke may be witty to a friend but rude to a stranger. So before joking, understand your audience first.

trans.ko:
칼럼
웃음의 기술

prompt.ko: 유머나 풍자에 대한 경험을 재치·오해·반응·교훈 순으로 4문장으로 써 보세요.
prompt.en: Write four sentences about an experience of humour or satire: the wit, a misunderstanding, the reaction, a lesson.

task.model: When a colleague joked with a straight face, I thought he was serious. It was actually tongue-in-cheek, but I took offence. Soon, realising the misunderstanding, I laughed it off. I learned that joking requires tact.

model_trans.ko: 동료가 무표정하게 농담을 했을 때 저는 진담인 줄 알았습니다. 그것은 사실 농담조의 말이었는데 저는 기분이 상했습니다. 그러나 곧 오해임을 알고 웃어넘겼습니다. 농담에는 눈치가 필요하다는 것을 배웠습니다.
model_trans.en: When a colleague joked with a straight face, I thought he was serious. It was actually tongue-in-cheek, but I took offence. Soon, realising the misunderstanding, I laughed it off. I learned that joking requires tact.
